drhp.business: The Company manufactures cement (blended cement and Ordinary Portland Cement) and, through its Hard Worker brand, a range of construction chemicals covering waterproofing, tiling, flooring, masonry, block fixing, repair, grouting and wall-finishing applications. It also runs a Wind Farm division and captive thermal and waste-heat power at its cement plants. Products are sold to residential, commercial, industrial, infrastructure, marine and precast construction demand through a dealer and sub-dealer network, serving both commercial (B2B) and private (B2C) customers including trade partners, …

drhp.expansion: Expansion in 2025-26 centred on Kolimigundla, debottlenecking of existing units, a new limestone block in Karnataka and the construction chemicals footprint. At Kolimigundla the railway siding was commissioned in July 2025 as previously indicated, and Line II - comprising 3.15 MTPA of clinkerisation, 1.50 MTPA of cement grinding and a 15.00 MW Waste Heat Recovery System - progressed with the cement mill commissioned in July 2025 and the rest of the project to be commissioned in 2026-27; clinker for Line II grinding will be met from Line I clinkerisation. risks.note: Cement production is carbon-intensive, with significant CO2 emissions from limestone calcination and fossil fuel combustion. The Company states escalating emissions would impact business continuity, attract regulatory scrutiny, increase compliance obligations and expose it to transition and physical climate risks affecting operational stability.
risks.risk: Greenhouse gas emissions and climate change

risks.note: Flagged as both risk and opportunity: dependence on coal-based captive power poses transition risks in a decarbonising economy with evolving regulatory frameworks, mitigated by transitioning away from coal-intensive generation and expanding wind and WHRS investment.
risks.risk: Energy management and dependence on coal-based captive power

risks.note: Operations span water-stressed and water-surplus regions requiring location-specific management. Water scarcity has demonstrated operational and community vulnerability affecting production continuity, and competing demands threaten operational stability and the social licence to operate.

Capital-intensive cement manufacturing carries inherent operational hazards; inadequate safety management may cause injuries, fatalities, legal liabilities, operational disruption, reputational damage and workforce morale erosion affecting productivity.

Brand equity and operational continuity are linked to supply chain resilience. Disruptions or reputational concerns from value chain partners may adversely affect material availability, production schedules and stakeholder confidence.

Current reliance on road transport for key materials generates significant Scope 3 emissions affecting the carbon footprint, and enhanced monitoring of transportation vehicles is required for oversight of routes, emissions, driver behaviour and safety compliance.
risks.risk: Sustainable supply chain and logistics - road transport dependence

risks.note: Operations and value chain engage large workforce populations - permanent employees, contract workers, transport partners and multi-tier suppliers - and systematic monitoring of transport partners and deeper-tier suppliers beyond contractual clauses requires enhanced due diligence.
risks.risk: Human rights across operations and the value chain

risks.note: Digital infrastructure underpins operational continuity, with enterprise systems directly controlling critical functions such as logistics dispatch and production management. Ransomware is identified as the primary threat, with potential system shutdowns, operational disruption, compromised intellectual property and data breach affecting stakeholder trust.
